HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Data: pl-catalogue (Fantasy Premier League, Understat, Opta via The Analyst, Transfermarkt), non-commercial, with attribution. Kickoff times and scores are checked against the Premier League's own fixture feed. European dates come from ESPN's public football schedule. Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. Each gameweek uses only the matches played before it. "Chance of the actual result" is the probability the model gave to what happened, averaged across the matches. Higher is better. Guessing at random lands near 33%.

HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Europe is Champions League, Europa League and Conference League matches so far. "Under 4 days" is how many league matches were played on fewer than four days' rest. xPts per match is points deserved on short rest, and on a normal week. The last column is rest before the next league match. The tag means a European game follows within five days. The League Cup and the FA Cup are not included.

HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Data: pl-catalogue (Fantasy Premier League, Understat, Opta via The Analyst, Transfermarkt), non-commercial, with attribution. Kickoff times and scores are checked against the Premier League's own fixture feed. European dates come from ESPN's public football schedule. Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Europe is Champions League, Europa League and Conference League matches so far. "Under 4 days" is how many league matches were played on fewer than four days' rest. xPts per match is points deserved on short rest, and on a normal week. The last column is rest before the next league match. The tag means a European game follows within five days. The League Cup and the FA Cup are not included.

HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Data: pl-catalogue (Fantasy Premier League, Understat, Opta via The Analyst, Transfermarkt), non-commercial, with attribution. Kickoff times and scores are checked against the Premier League's own fixture feed. European dates come from ESPN's public football schedule. Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. Read it the way an NFL efficiency table is read. When level: only the minutes the score was level. A side in front sits off, and a side behind commits players forward, so the score changes the chances they get. Good chances: the share of shots worth at least 0.10 xG, penalties excluded. Big chances: shots of at least 0.30 xG, per match. Green is better in the league, red is worse. A ° marks an Opta season total. Click a column heading to sort.

HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Data: pl-catalogue (Fantasy Premier League, Understat, Opta via The Analyst, Transfermarkt), non-commercial, with attribution. Kickoff times and scores are checked against the Premier League's own fixture feed. European dates come from ESPN's public football schedule. Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Data: pl-catalogue (Fantasy Premier League, Understat, Opta via The Analyst, Transfermarkt), non-commercial, with attribution. Kickoff times and scores are checked against the Premier League's own fixture feed. European dates come from ESPN's public football schedule. Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. The table is not the whole story. Who is actually playing well, and why.

ADJUSTED XG
OPPONENT AND VENUE REMOVED · AFTER GAMEWEEK 8

Raw xG flatters a side that plays at home, or that keeps meeting a weak defence. Each match here is divided by what an average club would create against that opponent, at that ground. Chances conceded are divided by that opponent's attack. What is left is the xG a club would have created and allowed against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Home advantage is worth about 10% more xG at the moment. Only this season's xG is used: not goals, and with no recency weighting.

HARDEST RUN

Sunderland have faced tougher grounds and tougher opponents than the rest. Adjusted, they are 0.54 xG per match better than the raw numbers (14th on raw xG, 9th once adjusted).

EASIEST RUN

The schedule flatters Man Utd. Adjusted, they are 0.35 xG per match worse than the raw numbers (10th on raw xG, 14th once adjusted).

BEST RIGHT NOW

Adjusted, Bournemouth lead the league: an xG difference of +0.96 per match against an average opponent on a neutral pitch.

Adj. is the opponent- and venue-adjusted figure. Diff. is adjusted xG minus adjusted xGA per match, which is what the ranking uses. Raw place is where the club would sit on the unadjusted xG difference. Home is home matches out of matches played.

HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Data: pl-catalogue (Fantasy Premier League, Understat, Opta via The Analyst, Transfermarkt), non-commercial, with attribution. Kickoff times and scores are checked against the Premier League's own fixture feed. European dates come from ESPN's public football schedule. Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. Click a column heading to sort, and click it again to reverse the order. Green is better in the league, red is worse. A big chance is at least 0.30 xG. npxG leaves penalties out. A ° marks an Opta season total, always from the latest file. Game state uses the minute of each goal. Points from comebacks: the win probability fell under 20% and the club still took something. Points spurned: the win probability was over 80% and the club did not win. A close match is a draw or a one-goal game. Those results are noisy, the same way close games are in the NFL, because they rarely repeat.

HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Data: pl-catalogue (Fantasy Premier League, Understat, Opta via The Analyst, Transfermarkt), non-commercial, with attribution. Kickoff times and scores are checked against the Premier League's own fixture feed. European dates come from ESPN's public football schedule. Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Data: pl-catalogue (Fantasy Premier League, Understat, Opta via The Analyst, Transfermarkt), non-commercial, with attribution. Kickoff times and scores are checked against the Premier League's own fixture feed. European dates come from ESPN's public football schedule. Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Data: pl-catalogue (Fantasy Premier League, Understat, Opta via The Analyst, Transfermarkt), non-commercial, with attribution. Kickoff times and scores are checked against the Premier League's own fixture feed. European dates come from ESPN's public football schedule. Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Data: pl-catalogue (Fantasy Premier League, Understat, Opta via The Analyst, Transfermarkt), non-commercial, with attribution. Kickoff times and scores are checked against the Premier League's own fixture feed. European dates come from ESPN's public football schedule. Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Data: pl-catalogue (Fantasy Premier League, Understat, Opta via The Analyst, Transfermarkt), non-commercial, with attribution. Kickoff times and scores are checked against the Premier League's own fixture feed. European dates come from ESPN's public football schedule. Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Data: pl-catalogue (Fantasy Premier League, Understat, Opta via The Analyst, Transfermarkt), non-commercial, with attribution. Kickoff times and scores are checked against the Premier League's own fixture feed. European dates come from ESPN's public football schedule. Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Data: pl-catalogue (Fantasy Premier League, Understat, Opta via The Analyst, Transfermarkt), non-commercial, with attribution. Kickoff times and scores are checked against the Premier League's own fixture feed. European dates come from ESPN's public football schedule. Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Data: pl-catalogue (Fantasy Premier League, Understat, Opta via The Analyst, Transfermarkt), non-commercial, with attribution. Kickoff times and scores are checked against the Premier League's own fixture feed. European dates come from ESPN's public football schedule. Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Data: pl-catalogue (Fantasy Premier League, Understat, Opta via The Analyst, Transfermarkt), non-commercial, with attribution. Kickoff times and scores are checked against the Premier League's own fixture feed. European dates come from ESPN's public football schedule. Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Kickoff times and scores are checked against the Premier League's own fixture feed. European dates come from ESPN's public football schedule. Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial.
