HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Data: pl-catalogue (Fantasy Premier League, Understat, Opta via The Analyst, Transfermarkt), non-commercial, with attribution. Kickoff times and scores are checked against the Premier League's own fixture feed. European dates come from ESPN's public football schedule. Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Data: pl-catalogue (Fantasy Premier League, Understat, Opta via The Analyst, Transfermarkt), non-commercial, with attribution. Kickoff times and scores are checked against the Premier League's own fixture feed. European dates come from ESPN's public football schedule. Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Data: pl-catalogue (Fantasy Premier League, Understat, Opta via The Analyst, Transfermarkt), non-commercial, with attribution. Kickoff times and scores are checked against the Premier League's own fixture feed. European dates come from ESPN's public football schedule. Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Data: pl-catalogue (Fantasy Premier League, Understat, Opta via The Analyst, Transfermarkt), non-commercial, with attribution. Kickoff times and scores are checked against the Premier League's own fixture feed. European dates come from ESPN's public football schedule. Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Data: pl-catalogue (Fantasy Premier League, Understat, Opta via The Analyst, Transfermarkt), non-commercial, with attribution. Kickoff times and scores are checked against the Premier League's own fixture feed. European dates come from ESPN's public football schedule. Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Data: pl-catalogue (Fantasy Premier League, Understat, Opta via The Analyst, Transfermarkt), non-commercial, with attribution. Kickoff times and scores are checked against the Premier League's own fixture feed. European dates come from ESPN's public football schedule. Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Data: pl-catalogue (Fantasy Premier League, Understat, Opta via The Analyst, Transfermarkt), non-commercial, with attribution. Kickoff times and scores are checked against the Premier League's own fixture feed. European dates come from ESPN's public football schedule. Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Kickoff times and scores are checked against the Premier League's own fixture feed. European dates come from ESPN's public football schedule. Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. Win probability added is how many expected points the player's goals were worth to the club at that moment, in the style of NFL win-probability added. Points added by goals is how many league points those goals were worth. Without them, the club would have had fewer. A winning goal is the one that put the club ahead for good. HAALAND · 30 SHOTS

HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

HAALAND · 30 SHOTS

HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Data: pl-catalogue (Fantasy Premier League, Understat, Opta via The Analyst, Transfermarkt), non-commercial, with attribution. Kickoff times and scores are checked against the Premier League's own fixture feed. European dates come from ESPN's public football schedule. Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. GROSS · 14 SHOTS

HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. RÚBEN · 5 SHOTS

HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Data: pl-catalogue (Fantasy Premier League, Understat, Opta via The Analyst, Transfermarkt), non-commercial, with attribution. Kickoff times and scores are checked against the Premier League's own fixture feed. European dates come from ESPN's public football schedule. Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. VERBRUGGEN · 0 SHOTS

HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Data: pl-catalogue (Fantasy Premier League, Understat, Opta via The Analyst, Transfermarkt), non-commercial, with attribution. Kickoff times and scores are checked against the Premier League's own fixture feed. European dates come from ESPN's public football schedule. Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. HAALAND · 30 SHOTS

HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Data: pl-catalogue (Fantasy Premier League, Understat, Opta via The Analyst, Transfermarkt), non-commercial, with attribution. Kickoff times and scores are checked against the Premier League's own fixture feed. European dates come from ESPN's public football schedule. Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. CHERKI · 15 SHOTS

HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Data: pl-catalogue (Fantasy Premier League, Understat, Opta via The Analyst, Transfermarkt), non-commercial, with attribution. Kickoff times and scores are checked against the Premier League's own fixture feed. European dates come from ESPN's public football schedule. Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Win probability added is how many expected points the player's goals were worth to the club at that moment, in the style of NFL win-probability added. Points added by goals is how many league points those goals were worth. Without them, the club would have had fewer. A winning goal is the one that put the club ahead for good. A solo goal has no assist and is not a penalty. Defensive contribution is the official Fantasy Premier League measure of tackles, blocks, clearances and recoveries. HAALAND · 30 SHOTS

HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Data: pl-catalogue (Fantasy Premier League, Understat, Opta via The Analyst, Transfermarkt), non-commercial, with attribution. Kickoff times and scores are checked against the Premier League's own fixture feed. European dates come from ESPN's public football schedule. Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%. A blown win is a draw in which one club was above 55% to win. Control is a deserved win with a clear xG gap. A comeback is a win in which the winner had been behind and their win probability had fallen below 25%. The lightning bolt is the excitement index: how far the win probabilities swung.

HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Kickoff times and scores are checked against the Premier League's own fixture feed. European dates come from ESPN's public football schedule. Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. ROBBERY

Click a match for the xG chart, the win-probability chart and every shot. The gameweek buttons at the top set the latest round included (now gameweek 8).

A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%. A blown win is a draw in which one club was above 55% to win. Control is a deserved win with a clear xG gap. A comeback is a win in which the winner had been behind and their win probability had fallen below 25%. The lightning bolt is the excitement index: how far the win probabilities swung.

HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Data: pl-catalogue (Fantasy Premier League, Understat, Opta via The Analyst, Transfermarkt), non-commercial, with attribution. Kickoff times and scores are checked against the Premier League's own fixture feed. European dates come from ESPN's public football schedule. Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. Click a match for the xG chart, the win-probability chart and every shot. The gameweek buttons at the top set the latest round included (now gameweek 8).

A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%. A blown win is a draw in which one club was above 55% to win. Control is a deserved win with a clear xG gap. A comeback is a win in which the winner had been behind and their win probability had fallen below 25%. The lightning bolt is the excitement index: how far the win probabilities swung.

HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Data: pl-catalogue (Fantasy Premier League, Understat, Opta via The Analyst, Transfermarkt), non-commercial, with attribution. Kickoff times and scores are checked against the Premier League's own fixture feed. European dates come from ESPN's public football schedule. Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial. Click a match for the xG chart, the win-probability chart and every shot. The gameweek buttons at the top set the latest round included (now gameweek 8).

A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%. A blown win is a draw in which one club was above 55% to win. Control is a deserved win with a clear xG gap. A comeback is a win in which the winner had been behind and their win probability had fallen below 25%. The lightning bolt is the excitement index: how far the win probabilities swung.

HOW THIS IS CALCULATED

xG is the chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken (Understat). A 0.10 shot scores about once in ten.

The chance bar and points deserved. From the shots in a match we calculate the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. Points deserved are 3 times the win chance plus the draw chance. A robbery is a win the shots rated below 30%.

Power and the forecast. Each club has an attack rating and a defence rating, fit to chances created and conceded (50% xG, 50% actual goals), adjusted for the opponent. Recent matches count for more: a match 6 gameweeks old counts about a third as much as this week's. Early in the season the ratings lean on a pre-season strength (the season file when one is supplied, otherwise earlier league results), and that anchor fades as this season's matches pile up. Match chances come from the two expected-goal figures (Poisson, with a Dixon–Coles adjustment that adds a few draws). The rest of the season is played 6,000 times.

Adjusted xG divides a match's xG by what an average side would create against that opponent, at that ground. Opponent strength and home advantage come from this season's xG only. Early on, those ratings are pulled gently towards the pre-season figure so one match cannot swing them.

True strength turns adjusted xG into the points that performance would be worth against an average opponent on a neutral pitch. Schedule and venue are the gap between that and the same sum from raw xG. Finishing and goalkeeping turn the gap between goals and xG into points. Whatever is left is other luck, so the pieces add up to the real points total.

Win probability, minute by minute, starts from the strength model before the round, then updates it for the score and the time left. Goals still to come follow a Poisson distribution. It does not see red cards or substitutions. The excitement index adds up how much the home and away win chances move.

Schedule and rest. The difficulty of a future match is the points the model expects from it. Rest is the time since a club's previous competitive match, including Champions League, Europa League and Conference League games loaded automatically. Domestic cups are not included, so a League Cup or FA Cup week can look quieter than it was. European kickoffs are loaded automatically (72 matches, 9 Premier League clubs). Domestic cup ties are not included, so a midweek cup game will not show up in the rest-day count. Clubs with no European tie this season are treated as not playing in Europe.

Game state is read from the goal times: how long a side led or trailed, points dropped from a winning position, points rescued from a losing one.

Opta numbers. PPDA is how many passes the opponent is allowed before a defensive action (lower means a more aggressive press). High turnovers are balls won within 40 metres of the opponent's goal. There are also directness and build-up counts.

Penalty xG used for non-penalty figures is the average of this season's 12 penalties (0.76), not a fixed number. The strength rating uses a goal level of 1.40 per team per match.

Data: pl-catalogue (Fantasy Premier League, Understat, Opta via The Analyst, Transfermarkt), non-commercial, with attribution. Kickoff times and scores are checked against the Premier League's own fixture feed. European dates come from ESPN's public football schedule. Pre-season strength is calculated here from historical Premier League and Championship results (football-data.co.uk). No bookmaker prices. Updated 2026-10-28, gameweeks 1–8. Independent, unofficial.
